Theme

Household, washing & chores

mess noun

untidiness, disorder

also messy, what a mess!, make a mess, mess up, in a mess, untidy, chaos (untidiness), make a mess of it

classical

Cic. Fam. 6.6.13: turba et cōnfūsiō rērum (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 345

turba, turbae f.

noun, first declension · Declension on Wiktionary

disorder, confusion, commotion

First the noise and jostle of a crowd, and so any disorder: turbās concīre, to make a mess of it (Traupman 345). Its everyday sense is a crowd, so make the context plain.

Other words

  • rēs turbulentae — a mess, a muddle

    noun phrase; in the exclamatory accusative, rēs turbulentās! · also used · classical · Plaut. Ep. 1.1.68 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 103, 345, 406

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut.)

    Plautus’s cry, which Traupman gives for “what a mess!”.

  • turbō, turbāre, turbāvī, turbātum — mess up, throw into disorder

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Quint. 11.3.148: nē comae turbārentur; M-O s.v. mess up · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Of hair, a table, plans: turbātus, messy, in disorder (Morgan–Owens, with incompositus).

  • squālor, squālōris m. — filth, dirt (a dirty mess)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 345; Plaut. Cist. 1.1.115 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    For a mess that is dirt rather than disorder; also sordēs (see dirt, grime).

Examples

  • heu edepol rēs turbulentās!

    oh lord, what a mess!Plaut. Ep. 1.1.68 (Lewis & Short)

  • nē comae turbārentur, quās compōnī vetuit

    so that his hair, which he had forbidden to be arranged, should not get messed upQuint. 11.3.148 (Lewis & Short)

  • Nihil hīc suō locō est!

    Nothing here is where it should be!composed

  • turbās conciēre

    to make a mess of it, to stir up troubleTraupman 345

  • Amphitruō āctūtum uxōrī turbās conciet

    Amphitryon will stir up a fuss with his wife right awayPlaut. Amph. 1.2.14 (Lewis & Short s.v. turba)

See also tidy up, dirty, dirt.
